claims.statement: Exposure to rising Chinese import competition due to the MFA quota removals reduced the number of years textile workers spent in mid-wage occupations over 2002-2009.

treatment.label: Import Competition (ImpComp = Exposure99ik x Posts), continuous exposure

outcome.label: Years of employment in mid-wage occupations (MIDeis)

quotes.text: leads to a signiﬁcant negative effect on mid-wage jobs at the same time that exposure to import competition increases employment in both high- and low-wage jobs.
Taking into account the average mid-wage employment of the control group over the post-shock years, which is 2.8 years, the 4.4 months amounts to a 13% reduction in mid-wage employment.

claims.statement: With a discrete (Yes/No) definition of exposure, working in 1999 at a firm producing quota-protected goods reduced years of mid-wage employment over 2002-2009.

treatment.label: Import Competition, discrete treatment definition (any quota product Yes/No) x Post

outcome.label: Years of employment in mid-wage occupations (MIDeis)

quotes.text: the results are similar when Import Competition is deﬁned as an indicator variable, equal to one if the worker was employed at a ﬁrm in 1999 producing at least one quota product
Taking into account the average mid-wage employment of the control group over the post-shock years, which is 2.8 years, the 4.4 months amounts to a 13% reduction in mid-wage employment.

claims.statement: Among mid-wage textile workers without college education, import competition reduced the number of years spent in mid-wage employment over 2002-2009.

treatment.label: Import Competition (ImpComp = Exposure99ik x Posts), continuous exposure

quotes.text: Column (1) of Panel A shows that import competition causes a signiﬁcant employment reduction in mid-wage occupations regardless of whether workers are college educated or not.

claims.statement: Among textile workers holding mid-wage occupations in 1999, import competition reduced the number of years spent in mid-wage occupations in the manufacturing sector over 2002-2009.

treatment.label: Import Competition (ImpComp = Exposure99ik x Posts), continuous exposure

outcome.label: Years of employment in mid-wage occupations in manufacturing (MIDeis)

source_table.value: Table 5, Panel A, row Manufacturing, column (1)

quotes.text: Column 1 of Panel A shows that the entire trade-induced reduction in mid-wage employment is driven by employment loss in the manufacturing sector.

claims.statement: Among textile workers holding mid-wage occupations in 1999, import competition caused a substantial reduction in mid-wage employment over the post-shock years.

treatment.label: Import Competition (ImpComp = Exposure99ik x Posts), continuous exposure

outcome.label: Years of employment in mid-wage occupations (MIDeis)

source_table.value: Fig. 3 (coefficients tabulated in Online Appendix Table B-7)

quotes.text: Fig. 3 shows that while Chinese import competition leads to a substantial reduction in mid-wage employment for these workers, the trade-induced increase in low-wage employment is on average larger than the increase in high-wage employment.
